verdict.rationale: Extend's single file-upload endpoint takes files for parsing, extraction and workflows. Its supported-file-types page lists PDF, images (PNG/JPG/TIFF), Excel (XLS/XLSX) and Word (DOC/DOCX), and Word or PowerPoint uploads are converted to PDF automatically, so no per-format plumbing is needed for those formats. HTML and email appear nowhere in the evidence, so two of the seven named formats are unconfirmed. Missing for 10: documented HTML support, documented email (EML/MSG) support, and independent hands-on confirmation of mixed-format processing through the API.

support.subject: As a developer, one API handles my whole document mix — PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, images, email — without per-format plumbing

citations.quote: We support the following file types: PDF .pdf Images .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .tiff ... Microsoft Excel .xls, .xlsx ... Microsoft Word .docx, .doc
If an uploaded file is detected as a Word or PowerPoint document, it will be automatically converted to a PDF.
This endpoint accepts file contents and registers them as a File in Extend, which can be used for running workflows, creating evaluation set items, parsing, etc.
